problem: Existing navigation world models (e.g. NWM) use multi-step diffusion with autoregressive frame-by-frame generation, so latency is prohibitive for planners that score many action candidates, and errors accumulate over long horizons. Prior work is mostly open-loop and image-goal only.
motivation: World models let robots imagine outcomes and reason spatially, which end-to-end policies (GNM/ViNT/NoMaD) lack. Real-time closed-loop use requires a fast world model, and a unified system for image, language and point goals would make world-model planning practical.
key_idea: Use a shortcut-model one-step generator with a 3D U-Net and decoupled spatial/window-temporal attention to predict all 11 future frames in one pass, and plug it into CEM planning with anchor-based initialization and goal-specific losses.
insight: Non-autoregressive one-step generation cuts inference time (0.076s vs 0.138s for NWM) and avoids compounding drift, and improves generation quality (PSNR 17.611 vs 14.557). Pretraining on the GNM dataset and random trajectory sampling both matter (generation ablations; image-goal SR 72.67 vs 64.00/64.67 without them). Anchor-based CEM initialization helps image-goal (72.67 vs 69.33 random init), and the language-goal loss is sensitive: SigLIP 69.33 vs CLIP 61.33 vs BLIP 59.33.
method: One-step world model: shortcut objective (flow matching at minimal step d_min, bootstrap consistency distilling two d/2 steps into one) conditioned on timestep t and step size d, so future latents are generated from noise in one step
3D U-Net architecture: pretrained SD VAE latent space; blocks of CNN, spatial attention and temporal attention; predicts 11 future frames simultaneously, non-autoregressively
Action embedding: N relative waypoints (x,y,cos φ,sin φ) go through a 4-layer MLP and condition the spatial attention via cross-attention
Window-based temporal attention: frame split into m×m spatial windows, and attention is computed across time only within the same window, reducing context length

Training strategy: pretrain on the GNM public navigation dataset, then fine-tune on 500 trajectories from the new scene; random trajectory sampling (random final frame plus 10 random intermediate frames)
CEM planner with anchor initialization: 32 samples, top 5, 5 iterations; initial candidates from fixed sets of linear/angular velocities

Goal-specific losses: LPIPS with a topological memory graph for image goals; SigLIP (instructions generated by Qwen2-VL) for language goals; point goals use Euclidean distance to target plus negative mean central depth from Depth-Anything on predicted frames

setting.backbone: 3D U-Net one-step (shortcut) world model with pretrained SD VAE, plus CEM planner; SigLIP / LPIPS / Depth-Anything as scoring modules
setting.training_data: Pretrained on the large-scale GNM navigation dataset, then fine-tuned on 500 trajectories per MP3D indoor scene collected in Habitat
setting.observation: monocular RGB (RealSense camera in real world)
setting.action_space: relative waypoints (x, y, φ) optimized by CEM; executed as linear and angular velocities

results: The world model beats NWM in generation (PSNR 17.611 vs 14.557) with about 45% less inference time. In simulation, image-goal SR is 72.67 (NWM 43.33, OmniVLA 36.67) and language-goal SR is 69.33 (NWM 51.33, OmniVLA 62.67). Point-goal SR is comparable to NWM (50.00 vs 52.67, which is higher). Real-world SR is 80/68/76% for image/language/point goals.
limitations: CEM must search the whole action space, which is hard for complex trajectories, and the iterative optimization trades off generation quality against speed
Planning latency is still about 0.8-1.3 s per step, and point-goal performance does not beat NWM
Evaluation is on a small self-collected setup (150 episodes, 5 scenes, 25 real trials per method) with per-scene fine-tuning
